title: Using machine learning for medium frequency derivative portfolio trading

extraction.methodology_summary: The authors construct a minimal risk portfolio of 5-year and 10-year US Treasury note futures using PCA weights. They extract daily trend features relative to weekly and biweekly moving averages, normalize them, and pass them through a Stacked Restricted Boltzmann Machine (Deep Belief Network) to learn latent representations. These features are then used by classifiers (SVM, Logistic Regression, and Neural Network) to predict the weekly direction of the portfolio, which is traded daily with a 5-day holding period.
extraction.data_period: daily data from 1985 (test set covers 2.5 years)
extraction.universe: 5 year and 10 year US treasury note futures (shortcodes ZF and ZN respectively)

key_findings: A machine learning pipeline using a Deep Belief Network (DBN) to extract features from technical indicators can successfully predict the weekly direction of a US Treasury note futures portfolio.
The SVM classifier achieved the highest test recall (60.00%) and test precision (62.58%) for predicting upward movements of the portfolio.
A day trading strategy based on these predictions generated approximately $90,000 in profit over a 2.5-year test period, excluding transaction costs and taxes.
The minimal risk portfolio constructed using PCA loadings (long ZF and short ZN) exhibits low drawdown and stable relative spread.
limitations: The bid-ask spread is ignored by using mid-prices.
The trading frequency is limited to a single trade per day.
The reported profitability of $90,000 excludes exchange transaction costs and taxes.
